title: Rotations Preserve the Dot Product
topic: An orthogonal matrix preserves the inner product: ⟨Ru, Rv⟩ = ⟨u, v⟩ for every pair of vectors. Sweep the rotation angle and watch the live dot product readout stay rock-steady while the two vectors swing together. This is what makes rotations 'rigid motions' — lengths, angles, and the geometric content of the inner product are invariant.

beats.narration: Rotate the whole picture. Does the dot product change?

elements.content: Spin the plane — does u · v survive?

beats.narration: Start with two vectors u and v. Compute their dot product and note the angle between them.

elements.content: u = (2.5, 0.5), v = (1.0, 2.0) on grid; arc shows angle between them

beats.narration: Multiply both vectors by the rotation matrix R of alpha. As alpha sweeps, both vectors swing together. Their dot product holds steady — the angle between them never changes.

elements.content: Both u and v rotated by R(α); α sweeps 0 → 2π smoothly
Live readout: ⟨Ru, Rv⟩ = 3.50 (constant); ‖Ru‖, ‖Rv‖ constant; angle between them constant
all three readings hold steady as α changes

beats.narration: Why? Because R transpose R equals the identity. The dot product is u transpose v — and the R cancels itself out inside.

elements.content: ⟨R u, R v⟩ = (R u)ᵀ (R v) = uᵀ Rᵀ R v = uᵀ I v = ⟨u, v⟩
the rotation cancels itself out — R is orthogonal

beats.narration: Rotations are rigid motions. Lengths, angles, dot products — all invariant. The geometry travels with the vectors.

elements.content: rigid motion — the geometry rides along
